name: Norway
sources: GDP $119.3bn and population 4.24m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series NOR, 1990 (119,344,377,526 and 4,241,473). Same series as the rest of the roster.

Oil 1.72 mbd: Norwegian crude production in 1990 was 1,716 thousand barrels a day (BP Statistical Review of World Energy). This is the second-largest producer in this roster's Western Europe after the United Kingdom's 1.9, on a fifteenth of the population, and it is the single most important number in this file - Norwegian output per head, Norwegian public finances and Norwegian politics for the next thirty years all run off it. The Government Petroleum Fund that this production paid for was legislated in 1990 and received its first deposit in 1996; nothing in this record schedules that, but the barrels that funded it are here.

Policy rate 11.5%: three-month Norwegian interbank rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 11.539% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TIB01NOM156N). High because the krone was pegged - unilaterally to the ECU from October 1990 - and because the Norwegian banking crisis was at its worst: the state took over Fokus Bank and Realkreditt in 1991 and Christiania Bank and Den norske Bank in 1991-92, wiping out the private shareholders of three of the four largest banks in the country.

Revenue 40% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Norway 1990 (about 40.2%). Understates the fiscal position, because petroleum revenue reaches the Norwegian state partly as direct ownership of production rather than as tax.
Gross public debt 29% of GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP, NOR 1990 = 29.1%. The lowest in this Western European batch and below Germany's 0.41.
Military 2.8% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), NOR 1990 = 2.834% - the highest of the Nordic four, above Sweden's 2.5 and Denmark's 2.0.

Strength index 9: about 34,000 active with a mobilisation strength near 285,000 out of four and a quarter million people, 170-odd Leopard 1s, F-16s, and a coastal artillery and submarine force built for the fjords. Indexed above Denmark's 6 and below Finland's 11. The reason is in the geography rather than the budget: Norway held NATO's only land border with the Soviet Union outside Turkey, 196 kilometres of it at Kirkenes, with the Northern Fleet's ballistic-missile submarines based two hours' drive away on the Kola peninsula. It is a small army guarding the most valuable ground in the alliance.

Gross fixed capital formation 23.0% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, NOR 1990. Split into public 3.5% and private 19.5% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual. CAVEAT: total transcribed, public share entered from reference knowledge of AMECO.

Stability 76 and authoritarianism 0.08: above France's 75, below Germany's 80. Norway is governed placidly and split down the middle by exactly one question. Jan P. Syse's Conservative-Centre-Christian coalition took office in October 1989 and fell on 29 October 1990 when the Centre Party walked out over the European Economic Area negotiations; the country had already voted no to European Community membership once, in 1972, and would do it again in 1994. A government falling over Europe inside the game's first year is the Norwegian pattern rather than an accident.
Separatism 0.01: none. The Sami Parliament opened in Karasjok on 9 October 1989 after the Alta dam protests, which is an accommodation reached rather than a movement running. Below France's 0.03.

TFP trend 0.014: at France's 0.014. Mainland Norwegian productivity growth through the 1990s was solid and unspectacular; the petroleum sector's contribution is a resource rent rather than productivity and does not belong in this number.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.4159%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series NOR (Norway): 4,140,099 in 1984 to 4,226,901 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 14.26 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, NOR, 1989: US$14259623106.89 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: NOR.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 86% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 167651 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: NOR, 1989 = 167651 subscriptions and 1990 = 196828 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: NOR, 1990 = 86%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
